regime: compiler-generated tensor-core kernels via torch.compile lowering of indirect Einsums; SpMM-COO is one worked example, no fixed matrix suite disclosed
rationale: Insum is a general indirect-Einsum compiler (SpMM/SDDMM/sparse-einsum all generated by the same lowering); README shows an SpMM-COO example but no named benchmark matrix suite, so it generates this kernel among others rather than being an SpMM-specific implementation.

regime: unstructured-sparse pruned LLM weights, ~30-90% density, fp16/bf16 Tensor Cores via CDP-TCBE bitmap decoding
rationale: Headline is an SpMM kernel (CDP-TCBE format) but built and evaluated for LLM inference weight sparsity; spec's general variant is SuiteSparse fp32, only the tensorcore-fp16 variant is in range.

regime: CPU sparse matrices from the ASpT/J-Stream/CSF-4 comparison literature (SuiteSparse-derived), fp32, all-physical-core OpenMP, median-of-50
rationale: RASSM's residue-based adaptive tiling is evaluated with dedicated SpMM-specific GFLOPS/median-time numbers against MKL/ASpT/J-Stream/CSF-4; spec's CPU variant (RASSM's own median-of-50 protocol) is explicitly modeled on this paper.

regime: pruned LLM weight matrices AND the SuiteSparse collection (per README's matrix_example/{pruned_weight,suite_collection}), kernel-level vs cuSPARSE, fp32 with an optional half-precision path
rationale: README confirms GeneralSparse benchmarks both pruned-LLM weights and genuine SuiteSparse .mtx matrices at kernel level against cuSPARSE (not just an LLM afterthought), so the general fp32 GPU-kernel variant is directly covered alongside the LLM-pruning niche.

regime: SuiteSparse/GNN benchmark matrices in the RoDe/DTC-SpMM/TC-GNN comparison lineage, fp32/tensor-core, unverified beyond convention
rationale: Voltrix is a general tensor-core SpMM kernel design (async loading, I/O-balanced partitioning) benchmarked directly against TC-GNN/DTC-SpMM/RoDe, the same comparison family DTC-SpMM's own artifact uses.

regime: general SuiteSparse-style sparse matrices vs cuSPARSE/Sputnik/dgSPARSE/TACO, fp32
rationale: LiteForm's CELL format and its auto-composition system are evaluated as a general SpMM kernel with GFLOPS speedups over cuSPARSE/Sputnik/dgSPARSE/TACO, not tied to any one downstream application.

regime: real-world graph datasets (single and batched graphs) feeding a fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM sparse-attention pipeline, H100/A30
rationale: SpMM here is one of three fused steps (3S) inside a sparse-attention kernel, evaluated as the fused pipeline and end-to-end Graph Transformer inference rather than as a standalone SpMM vs. cuSPARSE-class baseline.

regime: GNN training graphs (via PyG) and sparse-solve matrices (via MKL), CPU tile-fused loop kernels
rationale: Tile fusion is a compiler technique that fuses SpMM tiles with an adjacent parallel loop (GNN aggregation or sparse triangular solve); SpMM is one of the loop shapes it fuses/generates, and speedups are reported for the fused GNN-training and sparse-solve pipelines, not an isolated SpMM benchmark.

regime: binary (0/1) real-graph adjacency matrices for GNN inference, CPU shared-memory serial/parallel
rationale: CBM's headline contribution IS a compressed format + kernel for binary-matrix times dense-matrix multiplication, benchmarked directly against SOTA sparse-dense kernels; but it only handles 0/1-valued matrices, narrower than the spec's general real-valued SuiteSparse/GNN suite.

regime: N:M structured sparsity (e.g. 2:4/4:8 patterns), dense-format block matmul vs nmSPARSE and cuBLAS dense GEMM
rationale: NM-SpMM's headline is a general N:M-sparse matmul kernel evaluated at kernel level against nmSPARSE/cuBLAS, but N:M structured sparsity is a narrower regime than the spec's unstructured SuiteSparse/GNN headline.

regime: SuiteSparse/GNN matrices in the RoDe/DTC-SpMM comparison lineage, tensor-core, H100/RTX4090
rationale: FlashSparse is a general tensor-core SpMM/SDDMM kernel technique with geometric-mean speedups directly against RoDe and DTC-SpMM, the same matrix families those two use.

regime: SuiteSparse/GNN matrices (same family RoDe/DTC-SpMM use), transformed via matching+padding into 2:4 structured Sparse Tensor Core layout
rationale: MP-SpMM's headline is converting general unstructured SpMM into structured 2:4 sparsity and is benchmarked directly against RoDe/DTC-SpMM; the underlying matrices match the spec's suite but the executed format is structured Sparse-Tensor-Core, not the spec's general unstructured fp32/fp16 kernel.

regime: GNN adjacency graphs (15 benchmark datasets), evaluated end-to-end against GCN training frameworks (GNNAdvisor/PyG/DGL), no cuSPARSE/kernel-library baseline reported
rationale: StraGCN's Strassen-based SpMM is real and separable, but every reported speedup (2.1-3.3x) is against full GCN training frameworks rather than a standalone kernel vs. a vendor/kernel-level baseline.

regime: 3,000+ sparse matrices from established SuiteSparse-scale collections, 4 generations of Tensor Cores, structured+unstructured sparsity
rationale: SSpMM is a general tensor-core SpMM library benchmarked at kernel level across a very large matrix collection against the SOTA SpMM solution, squarely the spec's headline claim.

regime: 8-graph GNN suite (YeastH, OVCAR-8H, Yeast, DD, web-BerkStan, reddit, ddi, protein), origin+TCA-reordered, N in {128,256,512}, cuSPARSE/Sputnik/SparseTIR/TC-GNN baselines
rationale: Code-verified via run_DTC_SpMM.py (see survey.md #9): kernel is timed separately from one-shot TCA reordering, against vendor/kernel baselines on the exact GNN suite the spec's recommended_subset is built around.

regime: 24 real GNN benchmark graphs (README's maxk_graphs set), kernel-level vs cuSPARSE and GNNAdvisor kernels (spmm_maxk.cu / spmm_cusparse.cu / spmm_gnna.cu), but the dense operand is pre-sparsified by the MaxK top-k nonlinearity rather than fully dense
rationale: README confirms the artifact ships standalone SpGEMM/SSpMM kernels benchmarked directly against cuSPARSE/GNNAdvisor kernel binaries on a 24-graph suite, but the feature matrix is MaxK-sparsified (an algorithmic change to what SpMM operates on), a narrower regime than the spec's fully-dense operand.

regime: CPU multi-core SpMM vs Intel MKL, fp32
rationale: JITSpMM's whole contribution is a JIT-codegen technique specifically for the SpMM kernel, benchmarked at kernel level against MKL's SpMM routine.

regime: SuiteSparse .mtx directory, fp32/fp64, N in {32,128}
rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #8): RoDe cleanly separates preprocessing from the per-call kernel and reports GFLOP/s against Sputnik/cuSPARSE on SuiteSparse; this is the paper the spec's kernel-f32 variant is built around.

regime: 13 of the largest SuiteSparse matrices decomposed into arrow matrices, 100+ nodes / 128-GPU distributed scale, communication-volume metric not throughput
rationale: Headline IS a sparse-dense-matmul algorithm (arrow decomposition) evaluated against a prior SpMM algorithm, but at distributed multi-node/multi-GPU scale with communication volume as the metric; spec's notes_on_fairness explicitly excludes distributed SpMM as incommensurable with the single-node kernel variants.

regime: 9 curated SuiteSparse matrices (matrix_list.csv: mip1, shipsec1, pdb1HYS, consph, cant, cop20k_A, dc2, rma10, conf5_4-8x8-10), A100, M=N=K=512
rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #10): SMaT's own matrix list is exactly the recommended_subset's SuiteSparse cluster, benchmarked at kernel level via the raw MMA API against DASP/cuSPARSE/Magicube.

regime: standard GNN operator benchmark graphs, evaluated via a composable-format compiler generating SpMM/SDDMM/sparse-attention/sparse-conv kernels
rationale: SparseTIR is a sparse tensor compiler whose search space spans multiple operator classes (GNN ops, sparse attention, sparse conv); SpMM is one operator family among several the compiler targets and tunes, matching the compiler/DSL 'generates this kernel among others' case.

regime: GNN benchmark graphs (the TC-GNN/GNNAdvisor lineage the spec's recommended_subset traces back to), evaluated primarily as DGL-framework training speedup rather than standalone GFLOP/s
rationale: TC-GNN's sparse-graph-translation kernel is the ancestor of the exact 8-graph GNN suite this track's spec cites, and DTC-SpMM's own artifact runs TC-GNN's kernel as one of its parallel kernel-level baselines, evidencing a genuine separable SpMM/SDDMM kernel even though TC-GNN's own abstract reports only DGL-framework-level speedup.

regime: sparse matrices from real GNN applications, kernel-level plus embedded in GCN full-graph and GraphSAINT sampling training
rationale: HP-SpMM/HP-SDDMM are new standalone GPU kernels (hybrid vertex/edge parallelism) directly benchmarked against SOTA sparse kernel implementations before being embedded into GNN frameworks.

regime: block-structured (Shfl-BW) pruned DNN weight matrices, tunable density (e.g. 10%), Tensor-Core GEMM benchmark vs dense baseline, V100/T4/A100
rationale: README confirms a genuine standalone kernel benchmark (benchmark.spmm.out, A x B with a chosen block-sparsity density) rather than an end-to-end system, but the sparsity pattern is structured block-wise pruning for DNN weights, not the spec's general unstructured SuiteSparse fp32 regime.

regime: real GNN graphs, two-level (vertex/feature) parallel aggregation kernel evaluated end-to-end against full GNN computation systems (DGL/GNNAdvisor/FeatGraph)
rationale: TLPGNN's SpMM-like aggregation redesign is real and separable, but every reported number (5.6x/7.7x/3.3x) is a comparison against complete GNN computation systems, not standalone kernel throughput vs. a vendor/kernel library.

regime: mixed corpus (SuiteSparse + Network Repository + FROSTT + DARPA1998), CPU 64-core, TACO-generated fused loop-nest kernels
rationale: SparseLNR is a compiler (loop-nest restructuring for TACO) that generates fused kernels for multiple sparse tensor expressions, of which 2D SpMM (pdb1HYS, circuit5M, cora, bcsstk17) is one instance among 3D-tensor and other expressions.

regime: Erdos-Renyi random matrices + large real sparse matrices (100M+ edges), 256-node Cray XC40 CPU cluster, 1.5D/2.5D distributed communication-eliding algorithms vs PETSc
rationale: Headline IS distributed SpMM/SDDMM algorithms evaluated against PETSc's SpMM kernel, but the metric and scale (256-node communication time) are the distributed regime the spec explicitly separates from single-node kernel throughput.

regime: quantized int4/int8/mixed-precision SpMM on Tensor Cores, A100
rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #11): Magicube is the paper the spmm-gpu-quantized-int variant is modeled on, with per-iteration CUDA-event timing and an exact-match integer reference.

regime: CPU vectorized SpMM (alongside SpMV/SpTRSV) vs Intel MKL
rationale: LCM I/E's codelet-mining vectorization reports a dedicated SpMM speedup (1.75x avg) against MKL among its three target kernels, a genuine kernel-level comparison.

regime: GNN training graphs (Cora..YouTube, 10-80% training-vertex ratio), backward-aggregation-only partial-vertex SpMM isolated inside the full training-loop decomposition
rationale: Per survey.md #4, EPPGCN's own framing is explicit: SpMM/aggregation time is 'one component reported separately from total epoch time' of a whole-training-loop decomposition, not a standalone kernel microbenchmark, and it targets only the partial-vertex backward-aggregation sub-case.

regime: named real graphs (Cora..Orkut) + synthetic RMAT, 3 CPU architectures, fp32, MKL SpMM-only baseline plus DGL
rationale: Per survey.md #2 and spec.yaml's own cpu-kernel-f32 claim text, FusedMM is explicitly cited as one of the papers this CPU variant is modeled on; the paper isolates SpMM against an MKL SpMM-only baseline even though the kernel is fused with SDDMM for its primary use case.

regime: tile-wise structured sparsity, pruned DNN weight matrices, GPU tensor core, compared only against the dense model (no SpMM-library baseline)
rationale: Headline IS a co-designed sparse-matmul kernel/pattern, evaluated at kernel level, but on structured tile-wise DNN-pruning sparsity rather than the spec's general unstructured SuiteSparse regime, and against a dense baseline rather than SpMM libraries.

regime: real GNN graphs, composable sparse-templates+UDF backend generating GNN aggregation kernels, CPU and GPU
rationale: FeatGraph is a flexible backend that composes coarse-grained sparse templates with user-defined functions to generate various GNN aggregation kernels (of which SpMM-style aggregation is one instance), evaluated via end-to-end GNN training/inference speedup.

regime: SNAP graph collection + misc SuiteSparse-like matrices, CSR-native, fp32, N in {32..512}
rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #7): ITER=200 batched CUDA-event GFLOP/s vs cuSPARSE/Gunrock, the classic kernel-level SpMM benchmark this spec's variant descends from.

regime: Reddit + >1B-edge protein network, Summit >100 GPUs; wraps an unmodified cuSPARSE local SpMM kernel -- the contribution is the distributed communication schedule around it, not the kernel
rationale: Per survey.md #6, the paper's own text notes 'the SpMM kernel itself is not novel here, the contribution is the communication schedule'; CAGNET calls cuSPARSE via PyTorch without optimizing it, matching the 'kernel only touched, never optimized' tangential case.

regime: DNN-pruned weight matrices (3,012 matrices from real pruned ResNet-50/Transformer models via magnitude pruning, moderate ~70-95% sparsity), fp32 primary + fp16-mixed variant, V100
rationale: Per survey.md #1, headline IS a general SpMM/SDDMM GPU kernel library (ancestor of Sputnik, later used as a baseline throughout this track) evaluated at kernel level vs cuSPARSE, but its own test corpus is DNN-pruned moderate-sparsity weight matrices, not SuiteSparse-class matrices.

regime: LLM weight-tensor operand feeding a downstream GEMM, fused decompress-into-Tensor-Core-registers, GPU
rationale: Headline IS a lossless-compression format (TCA-TBE) + fused decompress-GEMM kernel, reported at kernel level (2.21x over cuBLAS) as well as end-to-end vLLM; this is exactly the structured-operand-fused variant's target case.

regime: multi-byte integer data (adaptive data mapping), CPU and GPU (A100/MI210)
rationale: Headline IS a general multi-byte ANS lossless encoder benchmarked at kernel-level throughput across CPU/GPU, matching the GPU multi-byte-integer variant's scope.

regime: X-ray light-source detector/sensor integer data, single-kernel GPU compressor, A100
rationale: Headline IS a single-kernel GPU lossless/lossy compressor for scientific sensor/detector streams -- the exact HPC-scientific multi-byte-integer domain this variant's summary names explicitly.

regime: unspecified HPC application datasets (five named), CPU multi-core, embedded in an MPI-collective compression-communication co-design
rationale: Abstract frames the lightweight CPU compressor as built 'in addition to' the paper's main contribution (a homomorphic compression-communication co-design for collectives); the compressor is real and separable but a component of the collective-communication system, and the evaluation is dominated by collective speedup, not standalone codec throughput.

regime: generic byte-stream corpora (Silesia corpus, base64-encoded data), CPU multi-core
rationale: Rapidgzip's headline IS a parallel gzip/DEFLATE decompressor benchmarked at kernel-level GB/s against GNU gzip on the Silesia corpus, exactly the generic byte-stream CPU variant's target.

regime: multi-byte GPU data (int16/int32/float), A100/A4000
rationale: Headline IS a GPU LZSS lossless compressor specifically designed for multi-byte data, benchmarked at kernel-level throughput/ratio against SOTA GPU compressors.

regime: SZ/cuSZ quantization-code streams (8 scientific datasets), V100
rationale: Headline IS an optimization of the Huffman-decoding lossless sub-kernel inside cuSZ, benchmarked at kernel level against cuSZ's own decoder -- exactly the SZ/cuSZ quantization-stream domain this variant's summary names.

regime: domain-specific-architecture-executed regex matching, MLIR-compiled binaries; execution-time/energy improvement over the same DSA's baseline compiler
rationale: The MLIR dialects target only regex matching (not a multi-kernel general compiler); this is a compilation-technique paper whose contribution is squarely regex-matching codegen, matching the compilation-amortized variant's description.

regime: large-scale automata workloads (20 applications), steady-state GPU matching throughput vs SOTA GPU automata engine
rationale: Headline IS a GPU automata-processing kernel technique (non-blocking symbol processing), evaluated as precompiled-automaton steady-state throughput, exactly the precompiled-kernel variant.

regime: multi-regex rulesets executed via FSA, CPU single/multi-threaded, compilation overhead reported separately from matching throughput
rationale: MFSA/iMFAnt's headline IS a regex-matching engine (automaton merging + execution), with matching throughput and compilation cost reported as separate numbers, matching the spec's precompiled-throughput vs. compilation-amortized split.

regime: real-world FSM workloads, GPU steady-state matching throughput vs SOTA GPU FSM parallelization
rationale: Headline IS a GPU FSM/regex-matching parallelization technique (speculation-centric scheduling) benchmarked at kernel-level throughput.

regime: NFA matching workloads, GPU steady-state throughput vs prior GPU NFA implementations and a domain-specific Automata Processor
rationale: Headline IS a GPU NFA-matching kernel optimization (read privatization, dynamic load balancing) evaluated at kernel-level throughput against both software and hardware (Automata Processor) baselines.

regime: exact-arithmetic scalability frontier under fixed time/memory budget (bit-sliced algebraic state encoding), tens of thousands of qubits, CPU
rationale: SliQSim is the paper this track's exact-arithmetic-scalability-frontier variant is built to isolate -- its claim is scaling accurate simulation, not steady-state gate-kernel throughput.

regime: gate-by-gate state-vector quantum circuit simulation, hybrid partitioner selecting per circuit pattern, GPU
rationale: HyQuas is explicitly named in the spec's state-vector/density-matrix gate-kernel variant as one of the four exemplar systems.

regime: random-quantum-circuit tensor-network contraction via slicing + path search, Sunway 42M-core distributed, mixed/single precision
rationale: SWQsim is the sole exemplar of the spec's rqc-tensor-network-contraction variant, a structurally distinct paradigm (contraction, not gate propagation) from the fp64 state-vector/density-matrix variant, and runs on Sunway (no NVIDIA GPU).

regime: gate-by-gate state-vector propagation, PGAS communication model across heterogeneous CPU/GPU backends (NVIDIA/AMD GPUs, multiple CPU vendors)
rationale: SV-Sim is explicitly named in the spec's state-vector/density-matrix gate-kernel variant; it includes an NVIDIA-GPU backend usable as a single-card kernel path.

regime: gate-by-gate density-matrix propagation, multi-GPU BSP communication scheme across GPU clusters (DGX-1/DGX-2/Summit)
rationale: DM-Sim is named in the spec's gate-kernel variant and the underlying gate operation matches, but the paper's own contribution and all reported speedups are about the multi-GPU BSP communication methodology (MG-BSP) rather than a single-card kernel path.

regime: autotunes existing black-box library parameter spaces (ScaLAPACK PDGEQRF, SuperLU_DIST, Hypre AMG) via crowd-sourced transfer learning; does not implement or modify the factorization kernel itself
rationale: GPTuneCrowd is a general cross-application autotuning framework; QR/LU factorization are unmodified library calls it tunes hyperparameters for, alongside an unrelated AMG solver -- it never touches the factorization algorithm or symbolic/numeric kernel.

regime: sparse direct LU factorization on real-world matrices, 2D block-cyclic distributed heterogeneous CPU systems
rationale: PanguLU's headline IS a sparse LU direct-solver algorithm (avoiding dense-BLAS fill-in waste), matching the numeric/e2e-amortized factorization variants; no GPU mentioned in this paper's own evaluation.

regime: symbolic LU factorization of nonsymmetric sparse matrices, GPU (scaled to multi-node Summit)
rationale: gSoFa's headline IS specifically the symbolic-factorization step of sparse LU, matching the spec's dedicated sparse-factor-symbolic-kernel variant exactly.

regime: multifrontal sparse QR factorization on real matrices, ARM/x86 CPU, vs SuiteSparseQR and MKL sparse QR
rationale: STM-multifrontal QR's headline IS sparse QR factorization performance (reordering selection + NUMA-aware task mapping), benchmarked at kernel level against vendor/library QR solvers.

regime: sparse SPD Cholesky factorization on real matrices, Sunway many-core CPU
rationale: swCholesky's headline IS sparse Cholesky factorization (supernode task queues + auto-tuning), matching the numeric-kernel factorization variant; no GPU.

regime: 30 real-world graphs, GPU biconnected components, both in-memory and out-of-core (edge-pruning skeleton)
rationale: Headline IS a GPU BCC algorithm with dedicated in-memory and out-of-core variants, matching the spec's cc-bcc-kernel-inmemory and cc-bcc-oom-external variants exactly.

regime: graphs of varying diameter (including large-diameter road-network-like graphs), CPU parallel biconnected components
rationale: Headline IS a space-efficient parallel BCC algorithm improving on Tarjan-Vishkin/BFS approaches, matching the spec's BCC in-memory variant (CPU side).

regime: power-law graphs and near-constant-degree mesh graphs (radiative transfer), GPU, A100
rationale: Headline IS a GPU strongly-connected-components algorithm, matching the spec's dedicated cc-scc-kernel variant.

regime: 2D and 3D binary image datasets (real + synthetic), GPU 8-connectivity labeling, YACCLAB benchmark
rationale: Headline IS a GPU 2D/3D connected-component-labeling algorithm on regular image grids, matching the spec's dedicated cc-image-ccl-2d3d variant exactly.

regime: large real-world graphs compressed via Elias-Fano encoding (primarily unweighted for BFS); SSSP and PageRank are stated extensions, not the depth-evaluated algorithm
rationale: The paper's headline contribution is a GPU-decompressible graph compression format evaluated in depth via BFS; SSSP is explicitly an added extension ('we also extend our work to...'), so it is a downstream application of the compression kernel rather than the headline SSSP algorithm, and its base format targets unweighted graphs.

regime: weighted directed graphs, GPU steady-state SSSP kernel, novel approximate priority-queue scheduler
rationale: Headline IS a GPU SSSP algorithm evaluated at kernel level against prior GPU SSSP work, exactly the spec's kernel-weighted-static variant.

regime: standard graph benchmarks including road networks with large diameters, CPU, SSSP is one of six ordered graph algorithms generated by the DSL
rationale: GraphIt's priority/bucket-fusion extension is a DSL that generates and optimizes several ordered graph algorithms (SSSP among them); comparisons are against Julienne/Galois/GAPBS on the standard ordered-algorithm benchmark set.

regime: sparse symmetric tensors, CPU, per-iteration S^3-TTMc/TTMcTC kernel vs SPLATT/CSS
rationale: SymProp is the paper the spec's tucker-symmetric-ttmc-kernel-fp64 variant is written around: it optimizes exactly the per-iteration TTMc/TTMc-chain kernel for symmetric sparse tensors.

regime: general (non-symmetric) sparse tensors, CPU/distributed, whole SGD-driven ALS-style decomposition loop
rationale: SGD_Tucker is the paper the spec's tucker-general-decomposition-e2e variant is written around: its headline algorithm IS the mini-batch stochastic decomposition loop, benchmarked against SOTA decomposition methods; no GPU.

regime: NTT/INTT over Z_q[x]/(x^N+1) with 32-bit RNS-CKKS moduli, always fused inside HMult/HRot/HAdd/Rescale ops or whole-FHE-workload runs, never timed in isolation
rationale: Cheddar's headline is a GPU FHE library with fused elementary-CKKS-op kernels; NTT is a real, well-defined sub-kernel but is architecturally never isolated, matching the spec's dedicated ntt-embedded-fhe-op variant rather than a standalone microkernel claim.

regime: mixed-type MoE grouped-GEMM operator (auto-synthesized GPU layouts) vs Triton; full token-routing/permute/gate-combine pipeline not detailed in the abstract
rationale: Hexcute is a general layout-synthesis compiler evaluated across GEMM, FlashAttention, and MoE operators; MoE is one benchmarked operator class among several the compiler targets, matching the compiler/DSL 'generates this kernel among others' case, and the reported number appears to be the grouped-GEMM piece rather than the full routing+combine MoE FFN.

regime: large real-world graphs exceeding single-GPU memory (>32GB / >12GB classes), multi-GPU (2-4 GPUs), vs single-GPU UVM baseline, MIS cardinality reported alongside throughput
rationale: MG-MIS's headline IS exactly the spec's single-node multi-GPU MIS problem, including the exact single-GPU-UVM baseline comparison the spec's second variant names; but the paper's own contribution requires multiple GPUs (the single-GPU UVM path is the pre-existing baseline, not MG-MIS's method), so per these instructions' single-card scope it reads false even though it is the track's defining paper.

regime: real-world graphs swept across degree/list-length skew, GPU degree-aware binned kernel with ML-based work distribution, plus a CPU multi-core algorithm from the same codebase
rationale: Headline IS exactly the spec's degree-aware binned Jaccard-weight kernel, with both the GPU and CPU baselines the spec's two variants call for, from the same codebase.

regime: real-world hypergraphs, shared-memory 72-core CPU, hypergraph betweenness centrality is one of ~8 algorithms (also MIS, k-core, hypertrees, hyperpaths, connected components, PageRank, SSSP) in an extended-Ligra suite
rationale: Shun20 does implement genuine parallel hypergraph BC (Brandes-style, matching the spec's semantics), but it is one algorithm among a broad general-purpose hypergraph-processing framework, not the paper's singular headline contribution.

regime: Tersoff potential + inter-layer potential (ILP) for layered materials (graphene, boron hexanitride), classical (non-learned) force field, CPU/Sunway many-core, weak-scaling to 2.7M atoms
rationale: LMFF's headline IS an optimized classical MD force/potential-energy kernel implementation (Tersoff/ILP) with large kernel-level speedups and weak-scaling results, matching the spec's classical-kernel and e2e-weak-scaling variants; no GPU (Sunway/Xeon only).

regime: Larger-Than-Life (LTL) cellular automata, radius sweep 1<=r<=16, tensor-core mapping vs CUDA-core baselines (naive/coarsened/shared-memory-tiled/bit-packed) from the same codebase
rationale: CAT is the paper this track's spec is written around almost verbatim: a tensor-core-mapped LTL CA implementation compared against CUDA-core baselines across a radius sweep, the exact axis the spec calls out.
